message.content: {"predictors": [{"name": "Short-Term Earnings Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the change in quarterly earnings growth rate: (most recent quarterly EPS - EPS one quarter ago) minus (EPS one quarter ago - EPS two quarters ago), divided by stock price.", "rationale": "Firms with accelerating earnings growth may signal improving fundamentals not yet fully incorporated in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Inventory Change Ratio", "construction": "Inventory change over past year divided by average total assets over the same period, using Compustat data.", "rationale": "Sudden increases in inventories can indicate poor sales prospects or overproduction, while decreases suggest strong demand.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Net Insider Buying", "construction": "Net purchases of shares by corporate insiders over the past six months, scaled by total shares outstanding, based on SEC filings.", "rationale": "Insider buying may reveal private information about undervaluation or future positive developments.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D Expense Ratio", "construction": "R&D expenditures divided by total sales over the past fiscal year, from Compustat.", "rationale": "Higher R&D spending may signal growth opportunities and management’s confidence in future prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Operating Cash Flow to Price", "construction": "Operating cash flow over the past year divided by current market capitalization.", "rationale": "Cash flow is less subject to accounting manipulation than earnings and may better capture firm health.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Consistency Score", "construction": "Number of consecutive years with non-decreasing regular dividends, as reported in CRSP and company reports.", "rationale": "Consistent dividends indicate stable earnings and disciplined management, reducing risk.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Volatility Skew", "construction": "Difference between stock’s 12-month daily return volatility and average industry volatility over the same period.", "rationale": "Stocks with idiosyncratic high volatility may be riskier or subject to mispricing.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Receivables Growth", "construction": "Annual growth rate of accounts receivable divided by sales growth over the same period.", "rationale": "Faster receivables growth than sales suggests earnings quality issues and potential collection problems.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Employee Productivity", "construction": "Total sales divided by number of employees at fiscal year-end.", "rationale": "Firms with higher productivity may be more efficient and profitable, supporting higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Price Reaction to Earnings Announcement", "construction": "Cumulative abnormal return over 2 days centered on most recent quarterly earnings announcement.", "rationale": "Stocks with muted price reactions may reflect delayed information incorporation and underreaction.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}]}
